newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia receives second British minesweeper.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia receives second British minesweeper.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has taken possession of a second British minesweeper as part of an oil-for-arms deal, a Western diplomat based in the Saudi capital Riyadh said on Wednesday.
"This is the second minehunter of three," he told Reuters. "It was accepted in the United Kingdom and will sail out in the coming weeks to Saudi Arabia."
The official Saudi Press Agency said the minesweeper had been received in the British port of Southampton on Tuesday.

The diplomat said the first of the ships, procured under the deal known as al-Yamamah, was delivered to Saudi Arabia early in 1996. The third and final vessel is to be delivered in 1997, he said, but no exact date was available.

In the mid-1980s, Riyadh turned to London for its defence needs after Washington turned it down. Saudi Arabia eventually awarded Britain two major oil-for-arms deals worth more than $20 billion for Tornado, Hawk and PC-9 military aircraft, specialised naval vessels and other hardware and services.
